transcript: Hi! I help businesses figure out exactly what they need from a chatbot. Before we start — what's your name?
Nice to meet you, Deirdre! What's the exact name of your business, as you'd want it written?
Lovely name, Deirdre. What's making you want a chatbot right now — what problem should it solve, or what's eating up your time?
People asking the same questions over and over. Prices, turnaround. That.
Makes sense. A few months from now, what would tell you this bot is actually working?
Good. Who are your customers typically — and are there different groups who tend to ask different things?
Brides mostly. Some ask prices, some ask timing. Same stuff really.
Got it. What kind of budget are you thinking for this, and any timeline in mind for getting it up and running?
Not sure. Cheap as possible. No rush.
Where's the business based — city or area — and do you have a premises customers actually visit, or is it all online/by appointment?
Kilkenny. Garage, sort of. Not really visitors.

Before we dive into pricing details — if you've got any real customer chats or emails handy (screenshots or exports), sharing a few would help me ask much sharper questions. You can drop them in the 'uploads' folder next to this program and just tell me when done. If that's a hassle, no worries — we can carry on without them. Want to try, or shall we skip it?
No problem. So, what do you actually offer — what are all the products or services Thistle & Ink Press sells?
Wedding invites. Save-the-dates. Place cards. That sort of thing.
Great, that's a good core list — anything else you offer or charge for, even smaller or occasional jobs, besides invites, save-the-dates and place cards?
Let's start with wedding invites — what's the price range you typically quote for those?
Good to know. Does that price change with quantity (more or fewer than 50 sets), or with different paper/design options?
Custom illustrated ones start at 650. Minimum order's 30.
Got it — standard from €480/50, custom illustrated from €650, 30-set minimum. What's the usual turnaround time for wedding invites, start to finish?
When it's peak season, roughly how much longer does that turnaround stretch — and what should the bot tell a bride asking during that busy stretch?
10-12 weeks. March to June, that is.
Noted — peak season March to June runs 10-12 weeks. Now, save-the-dates: what's the price range and typical turnaround for those?
90 a pop for 25. Add-on, really. Turnaround's same as the invites.
And place cards — what do those go for, and what's the turnaround?
Not sure, actually. Don't get asked much.
That's fine — if a bride does ask about place cards, should the bot just say to contact you directly for a quote, or is there a rough starting price you're comfortable giving?
Do you take deposits on orders — and if so, how much, and what payment methods do you accept?
Got it — 50% to book, rest before shipping. What payment methods do you accept?
That's fine, bank transfer as the main one it is. Do you offer any refunds or cancellations if a bride changes her mind after booking?
No refunds once plates are cut.
Understood. Do you offer any kind of guarantee — like reprints if there's a printing error or damage in transit?
Not really thought about that. Depends on the case.
Fair enough — so if a bride messages about a printing error or damage, should the bot just say to contact you directly to sort it out, case by case?
Is it just you running things, or is there anyone else helping — even part-time?

Good to know. When a customer question needs a human — like a dispute or a tricky order issue — should the bot point them to you directly, and what's the best way for them to reach you (phone, email, WhatsApp)?
Ring me. Or the whatsapp-thing, I s'pose.
What's the actual phone number (or WhatsApp number, if different) the bot should give customers?
Eh... 087 something. I'll dig it out and send it on.
No worries, just send it whenever you have it. Now — what channels do you want this bot working on? Website chat, WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, something else?
Website, I s'pose. Maybe the whatsapp-thing too.
Good. Roughly how many customer messages or emails would you say you get in a typical week?
That's fine, a handful a week is a good ballpark. Just English for the bot, or other languages too?
Since there's no shop customers visit, are there set hours you're generally reachable or working — for the bot to reference if someone asks?
Tuesday to Friday, ten to four. Studio hours anyway.
Good. And do you want this to be a simple bot that just answers questions and gives info, or something fuller that handles bookings/payments too?
Just answers, I think. Keep it simple.

Simple it is — just answering questions, no bookings built in. During peak season (March-June) when things get busy, is there a point where you'd want the bot to warn brides that turnaround might be even longer, or to stop taking new orders altogether?

brief.business_description: Based in Kilkenny; works out of a garage/workshop, not really set up for visitors. Team: Deirdre (owner) and niece Aoife, who helps Tuesdays/Thursdays with packing.
brief.problem_to_solve: Customers repeatedly ask the same questions (prices, turnaround times), which takes up Deirdre's time.
brief.target_audience: Mostly brides; questions tend to be about prices or timing.
brief.conversation_volume: Estimate: a handful of customer messages/emails per week (owner unsure of exact number)
brief.budget: As cheap as possible (no specific figure given)
services_and_pricing: Wedding invites (standard) - €480 for 50 sets - turnaround 6-8 weeks normally, 10-12 weeks during peak season (March-June)
Wedding invites (custom illustrated) - starts at €650 - turnaround 6-8 weeks normally, 10-12 weeks during peak season (March-June)
Save-the-dates - €90 per 25 - usually an add-on to invites - turnaround same as invites (6-8 weeks normally, 10-12 weeks peak season)
Place cards - no set price/turnaround; bot should tell customer to contact Deirdre directly for a quote
faq_answers: Place cards pricing/turnaround: bot says 'contact me directly for a quote' (rarely asked about, no standard pricing)
Printing errors/damage: bot says to contact Deirdre directly to sort it out, handled case by case
business_policies: Deposit: 50% required to book an order; remaining 50% due before shipping.
Payment method: mostly bank transfer; owner unsure of other accepted methods.
Refunds: no refunds once printing plates are cut.
Reprints/damage guarantee: no fixed policy — handled case-by-case; bot tells customer to contact Deirdre directly.
escalation_rules: For disputes/tricky issues, bot should direct customer to phone Deirdre or reach her on WhatsApp. Exact number pending — owner to send it on.
open_items: Deirdre's exact phone/WhatsApp number for escalation — she'll send it on.
additional_notes: Peak season is March to June, when turnaround stretches to 10-12 weeks.
Bot scope: simple Q&A / info bot only — no booking or payment handling.
